drawing_priorities: head direction from pupils and nose
balanced face, spine, shoulder and pelvis line hierarchy
one centre-path curve per limb through its joint centres
evidence_refs: p1_target.png user-approved task-stage target normalized to 512x802

global_relations.canvas_basis: All listed coordinates were observed on the 512x802 working canvas.
global_relations.head_direction: slight turn toward image-left with a small downward tilt
global_relations.pelvis_tilt: image-left hip higher; image-right hip lower
global_relations.shoulder_tilt: image-left shoulder lower; image-right shoulder higher

feet.image_left: weight-bearing shoe points across the body toward image-left
feet.image_right: lower stepped-out shoe points toward the viewer and image-right

observation.subject_summary: Full-body front three-quarter standing subject. The image-left leg carries the weight; the image-right leg steps out. The image-left arm hangs while the image-right arm bends into the trouser pocket.
uncertainties: Loose denim obscures exact knee contours; knee centres are inferred from each hip-to-ankle chain.
The pocket and sleeve partly hide the image-right wrist and hand endpoint.

subject_left: wrist partly covered by cardigan cuff

uncertainties: Near-side assignment follows the larger image-right sleeve and shoulder exposure.

notes: The listed order is review sequence, not a geometry override hierarchy.
Task stage targets state intended same-task stage representation and placement.
Subject reference remains geometry and visible-edge truth and resolves contradictions about pose/proportion/perspective/overlap.

must_not_decide: which construction convention belongs to a stage
facts that contradict the subject reference
generic stage grammar outside the current task
